newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on swaps, JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on swaps, JGBs.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract ended higher on Wednesday as short positions were squeezed by falls in interest rates across the spectrum, traders said.

Banks actively bought fixed interest rates of up to seven years in the swap market. Institutional investors were active buyers in the JGB market on market conviction that the Bank of Japan will hold interest rates down for a while.

At the outset, euroyen prices were pressured by a recovery in Japan's stock market following Tuesday's news that the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) would form a strategic alliance, traders said.
This means Japan's ailing banking sector has been relieved of one negative factor, traders said.
Some said there had been speculation that the LTCB may withdraw from some overseas operations.
However, traders covered short positions by midday as the LTCB-SBC tie-up news did not point to a near-term credit tightening by the BOJ, they said.

Meanwhile, Moody's Investors Service Inc said on Tuesday it will continue a review of the debt ratings of LTCB for possible downgrade despite the announcement of the bank's strategic alliance with SBC.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told reporters on Wednesday that the central bank's money policy management focuses on overall economic activities, not a specific sector or industry.
But the market mostly ignored Matsushita's remark.
The key overnight call rate was at 0.53-0.54 percent, up from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.52 percent, in response to traders' disappointment at the BOJ's neutral operation stance.

The BOJ fully offset a projected shortfall by providing 200 billion yen to the market. Some traders had expected a fund injection of up to 300 billion yen by the central bank in view of a rise in the call rate on Tuesday from 0.51 on Monday.
The BOJ is likely let the market have some 100 billion yen in surplus on Thursday to offset upward pressure in the short end of the market, traders said.
In the longer end of the money market, the key three-month certificate of deposit was traded at 0.66 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
